findings.writer: SETTLED. State value 3 is written by exactly one body: the unpark body 0x5ce3580..0x5ce3662 of the vendored tokio multi-thread scheduler park module. Its entry loads 3 (pin 0x5ce3585) and xchgs it into the state word at [handle+0x18] (pin 0x5ce358a) -- the word the contention fallback packet fixed as [Q+8] of the per-thread park cell, reached here through the handle object whose +0x10 field is Q. The body's one panic carries the multi_thread/park.rs line 288 Location (static 0x64c5a38) and the message piece "inconsistent state in unpark; actual = ". The whole-.text scan for the store pattern (immediate 3 loaded for an xchg into a +0x18 word) finds this site alone, and the module Location census names every body of the module -- wrapper_state 0x5ce2fd0, the contention fallback 0x5ce30d0, registration_b 0x5cec8b0 and this unpark -- of which the first three only consume 3 with the CAS 3 -> 0 sites the earlier packets pinned.
findings.old_value_arms: SETTLED. The swap's old value is switched through the jump table at 0x94cb20: 0 -> 0x5ce35c7 (return; the 3 stays latched as a pending notification), 1 -> 0x5ce35a4 (claim the guard byte at [handle+0x28] = [Q+0x18] with CAS 0 -> 1, pin 0x5ce35a8, waiting on it through GOT 0x64e01f8 / byte_wait 0x5bb59d0 with the sentinel on contention; release with CAS 1 -> 0, pin 0x5ce35b3, calling byte_notify through GOT 0x64e0f38 when the release fails; then if the wait-key word at [handle+0x20] = [Q+0x10] is non-zero, tail-jump through GOT 0x64ec188 to the wake body 0x5bb42e0 with (&key, token)), 2 -> 0x5ce35cd (forward the second argument and tail-jump to the driver signal body 0x5ce09a0), 3 -> 0x5ce35c7 (already notified; return). An old value above 3 takes the line-288 panic at 0x5ce35da with the old value as the {} argument; no writer in the pinned graph produces a value above 3.
findings.inner_arm: SETTLED. The driver signal body 0x5ce09a0..0x5ce0aa2 is an inline copy of the runtime-park unpark protocol on the shared inner, reached only from the unpark body's old == 2 arm with rdi = the caller-supplied slot pointer (ctx+0x150, or ctx+0x160 in the broadcast caller). It dereferences the slot and swaps 2 into the inner parker state word at [inner+0x10] (pins 0x5ce09c2/0x5ce09c7): old 0 or 2 returns, old 1 claims the inner byte at [inner+0x20] (pin 0x5ce09f9), snapshots the token at [inner+0x18] (pin 0x5ce0a0b) and tail-jumps through GOT 0x64ec188 to the wake body (pin 0x5ce0a20), and any other old value panics through the runtime/park.rs line 187 Location (static 0x64c6f60) the TLS value-object packet pinned for the out-of-line unpark 0x5cfd600 -- the same protocol, inlined at the driver's call site.
findings.entry_points: SETTLED. Exactly six direct references, no indirect route: no .rela.dyn RELATIVE addend names the body and its start occurs nowhere in the file as a stored pointer. Five callers resolve the target cell out of a scheduler context first -- claim the byte at [ctx+0xf8], bounds-check the index against [ctx+0x90], load the handle from the 16-byte table at [ctx+0x88] (entry +8), pass ctx+0x150 as the second argument: signal_arg 0x5ce3fd0 (tail jump 0x5ce4235, index from a register), signal_pop_call 0x5ce4430 (call 0x5ce450e), signal_pop_jmp_a 0x5ce45b0 (tail jump 0x5ce468f), signal_pop_jmp_b 0x5ce4720 (tail jump 0x5ce48cb) and signal_pop_call_b 0x5ce4990 (call 0x5ce4a88) -- the four pop variants take the index from the top of the context stack at [ctx+0x108]/[ctx+0x110]. The sixth, signal_all 0x5cfadf0 (call 0x5cfaec8 in its loop), unparks every entry of its own table ([ctx+0x98]/[ctx+0xa0], second argument ctx+0x160). A wake therefore targets exactly the cell whose handle the caller resolved; the unpark body itself is cell-agnostic.
findings.handle_neighbour: CONTEXT. The body immediately above the unpark, handle_clone 0x5ce3430..0x5ce3578, builds a fresh handle-sized allocation pair (0x58-byte block copied from its argument, 0x30-byte block holding the two 1-valued header words and the block pointer) through the allocator slot 0x64df480; it is pinned here as the unpark body's extent neighbour and the handle factory of the same cluster, and no claim about its callers is made.

open_edges: What distinguishes the four pop-variant signal bodies (0x5ce4430, 0x5ce45b0, 0x5ce4720, 0x5ce4990) from each other beyond index source and call-vs-tail-jump -- e.g. which scheduler event each one serves -- is not traced here.

The writers of the scheduler context fields the signal bodies read (the worker table at ctx+0x88/+0x90, the index stack at ctx+0x108/+0x110, the guard byte at ctx+0xf8, the inner slot at ctx+0x150) are not censused here; the forwarder time-context writers edge of the park_timeout provenance packet is the same shape of question for the time context.
Open edges 1 and 4 of the TLS value-object packet (the parking layer bit protocol and the missing type name) and the [S+0x50] byte-claim census edge of the contention fallback packet remain open.
